title: Equal Sum Split
statement:
Can the numbers in `numbers` be split into **two groups with exactly the same total**? Every number must go into exactly one of the two groups.

Return `true` if that is possible, otherwise `false`.

examples.explanation: Groups {11} and {1, 5, 5} both add up to 11.
The total is 11, which is odd, so two equal halves are impossible.

hints.nudge: If a valid split exists, one group has a total of exactly half of everything. When is that half not even a whole number?
hints.pattern: Subset sum: can some of the numbers add up to exactly total / 2? Track which totals are reachable.
hints.walkthrough: Two groups with equal totals means each group adds up to total / 2, so an odd total is an immediate no. Otherwise the question becomes: can a subset of the numbers add up to exactly half? Keep a table of reachable subset totals, starting with only 0 reachable. For each number x, every total s that was reachable before also makes s + x reachable; loop the totals DOWNWARD so that each number is used at most once. When the loop ends, check whether total / 2 is reachable. O(n * total) time and O(total) memory; in Python a big integer used as a bitset (reach |= reach << x) does the same much faster.
